module_title: Variation of 'g', Kepler's Laws, and Escape Velocity
introduction: The Earth is not a perfect sphere (it bulges at the equator), and it is constantly spinning. Because of this, gravity is not uniform everywhere. This level explores these variations and the physics of escaping a planet's gravity.

core_concepts.title: Variation in the value of 'g'
core_concepts.description:
1. At the Equator: The value of $g$ is 'Minimum'. 
2. At the Poles: The value of $g$ is 'Maximum'. (Hence, an object weighs slightly more at the poles than at the equator). 
3. Altitude & Depth: The value of $g$ 'decreases' when you go high above the surface OR deep into a mine. 
4. Center of the Earth: The value of $g$ is exactly 'ZERO'.

core_concepts.title: Escape Velocity ($v_e$)
core_concepts.description:
The minimum velocity required to project a body vertically upward so that it never returns to the surface of the planet (it escapes the gravitational field). 
Formula: $v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$. 
Escape Velocity for Earth: $11.2 \text{ km/s}$.

core_concepts.title: Why does the Moon have no atmosphere?
core_concepts.description: The escape velocity on the Moon is very low ($2.38 \text{ km/s}$). The thermal velocity (speed) of gas molecules there is higher than this escape velocity. Hence, all gases simply escape into space. This is a highly repeated conceptual question in NDA.

core_concepts.title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
core_concepts.description:
1. Law of Orbits: All planets move in 'Elliptical' orbits with the Sun at one of the foci. 
2. Law of Areas: Planets move 'faster' when they are closer to the Sun and 'slower' when they are farther away. 
3. Law of Periods: The square of the time period of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of its average distance from the Sun ($T^2 \propto R^3$).

important_entities.name: Effect of Earth's Rotation on 'g'
important_entities.significance: If the Earth starts spinning much faster on its axis, the value of $g$ at the equator will 'decrease' further. If the Earth suddenly stops spinning, the weight of objects everywhere (except at the poles) will 'increase'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Escape Velocity is Independent of Mass
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'If a 10 kg stone and a 100 kg boulder are thrown, will their escape velocities differ?' FALSE! Escape velocity ($v_e$) is 'independent' of the mass of the projected body. It is $11.2 \text{ km/s}$ for both an ant and an elephant.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Since the poles are slightly closer to the center of the Earth (due to its flattened shape), the gravitational pull ($g$) is at its peak (maximum) there.

exam_strategy_tips: A classic Railway exam question: 'What will be the weight of a body at the center of the Earth?' Since $g=0$ at the center, the weight ($W = m \times 0$) will be ZERO.
